_leadership_summary:
Over the January–July 2026 period, the national portfolio improved materially, with average Win Score rising from 3.19 in January to a peak of 3.36 in June before settling at 3.32 in July — a net gain of 0.13. The improvement was driven almost entirely by two components: Win Score, which climbed from 2.8 to 3.05 (+0.25), and Hutbot Ontime, which strengthened from 3.54 to 3.91 (+0.37). FSCC remained the portfolio's clear strength, holding between 4.82 and 4.88 all period, while Brand was flat at 3.33. Tier migration reflects this momentum: Tier 1 stores fell from 1,015 to 845, Tier 3 expanded from 851 to 1,069, and 1,107 stores moved up versus 730 moving down. Zone leadership was led by Dustin Patton at 3.72 average, with the strongest absolute improvement from Danielle Hudson (+0.32, Tier 3 share up 76.9%), AKM Shaju (+0.24, Tier 3 up 53.1%), and Sergio Villasenor (+0.18). At the opposite end, Paul Inacio was effectively flat at +0.01 (his Tier 3 share declined 5.0%), with Derron Spencer (+0.05) and Hellen Lobaccaro (+0.06) rounding out the weakest improvement.

Portfolio health is improving but uneven. Current national average stands at 3.32, with 845 stores in Tier 1, 2,770 in Tier 2, and 1,069 in Tier 3. Zones requiring the most attention are Kathleen Basbagill (2.90 average), Sergio Villasenor and Sarah Heitz (both 3.06), and Finley Klement (3.09); notably, Cellesha Steel and Michael Grant each cut Tier 1 share sharply (0.0% and −44.8% respectively) even as their averages lag. The binding-constraint analysis shows a clear tier progression: in Tier 1, Win Score is the binding constraint in 63.7% of stores, with Speed at 27.5%; in Tier 2, Win Score falls to 43.7% while Speed rises to 33.9%; and in Tier 3, Speed (35.7%) edges out Win Score (31.5%) and Brand (29.8%) as the leading limiter. Risk exposure remains a concern — 274 stores are in default status, 29 are at risk, and 452 are on the Tier 1 watchlist — and the weak correlation between 5-Star performance and same-store sales growth (0.10 SSSG, 0.11 SSTG) indicates that operational excellence is not yet translating into growth.

Franchisee rankings show a wide performance spread. The top five by average score are AL SALAS (4.09 across 49 stores), MARK PETERSON (4.05, 68), DOUGLAS CLEVELAND (4.03, 18), HEMANG CHAMPANERIA (3.97, 2), and CRAIG ERIKSON (3.74, 34). The bottom five are ASAD ADAM MITHA (1.70, 7), JAKE RASOR (1.85, 1), KETANKUMAR PATEL (1.87, 29), and RUSS KLUG and ROBERT CORONADO (both 2.14, 2 and 1 stores respectively). Notably, three of the bottom five (Mitha, Rasor, Patel) and the top three all report to the same director and field team, suggesting performance is operator-specific rather than zone-driven, and Ketankumar Patel's 29-store footprint at 1.87 represents the highest systemic exposure in the bottom group.

The primary national priority is Speed of Service. It is the only component in decline (2.94 → 2.84), the weakest major metric against the portfolio's 3.32 average, and — critically — it becomes the leading binding constraint as stores improve, which will cap Tier 3 progression and stall future tier migration. Recommended operational focus areas are peak-period throughput and kitchen expediting, drive-thru and service-time coaching at Tier 1 and Tier 2 stores where Speed is already binding at 27.5% and 33.9% respectively, and targeted support for the 452-store watchlist before they cascade into default. With Win Score, FSCC, and Hutbot already delivering, closing the Speed gap is the clearest lever to move the national average toward Tier 3 parity.
